title: Road-event task, temporal input and evaluation protocol
why: Define agent-action-location compositions, candidate boxes, the eight-frame window, and training-derived tail groups before model comparisons.
caption: ROAD-Waymo event recognition associates a candidate box at time t with agent, action, location and valid composition labels. The CSEB visual window includes t-3 through t+4; detector evaluation uses fixed candidates and frames, while head training and checkpoint/blend selection use distinct recorded partitions.
evidence: Locked 36,717-frame protocol; 184 outputs include agentness; Tail47 and Deep28 are derived from training counts.
action: Compose a journal-sized task/protocol figure from the existing crop and frame-map ancestors; inspect annotations before choosing the example. Do not imply causal or real-time inference.

title: Why move beyond local scoring? Selected crop baselines
why: Three aligned panels distinguish phrase scoring, visual composition and explicit phrase-score fusion without reproducing every historical experiment.
caption: Selected actor-crop baselines: (a) semantic phrase classifier; (b) crop features and primitive scores with a composition MLP; (c) additional phrase-composition evidence. These are historical architectural alternatives, not isolated single-factor comparisons with CSEB.
evidence: Workbook models57/59/60: triplet9.065/11.226/11.275; tail5.775/6.164/6.168. Stage5 does not consume phrase-composition scores; Stage6 does.

title: CSEB: complete inference architecture
why: Give the reviewer one definitive view of the chosen model and identify what is inherited versus contributed.
caption: CSEB combines actor-crop, RoI, scene-token and geometry representations in two contextual experts. Both experts contain scene and language attention. Their135 composition probabilities are blended using a selection-set weight; classification-expert primitive scores are retained before detector assembly. Frozen video/text encoders are shared feature sources, not separately trained expert backbones.
evidence: Scaled CSEB:15.748±0.274 triplet,9.000±0.644 Tail47,6.354±0.571 Deep28, three seeds. Visual width1408, phrase bank184×768, head width512.
action: Use the approved editable CSEB ancestor. For the journal, clarify that duplicated encoder drawings denote shared weights and explain the InternVL text-checkpoint provenance in the caption/methods. Do not label its text tower as having1B parameters.

title: Actor-conditioned scene attention versus mean pooling
why: Explain why an actor should select relevant scene context instead of receiving one indiscriminate scene average.
caption: Both contextual heads fuse crop, RoI, scene and geometry evidence. The mean-pool variant averages scene tokens; scene attention uses crop plus box position as its query and scene tokens as keys and values. Language attention follows visual fusion and is a distinct operation.
evidence: Matched focal classification study, models88/89: triplet11.740→12.024; Tail47 5.473→6.189. Report paired seed variability before making a significance claim.
action: Make a two-panel close-up retaining shared geometry. This figure tests scene aggregation; it does not establish separate crop/RoI/geometry component effects.

title: Expert training objectives and gradient paths
why: Explain precisely how the two experts differ and why the contrastive branch is a training objective rather than another inference input.
caption: The classification expert minimizes the implemented difficulty-calibrated classification objective. The second expert adds a multi-positive auxiliary aligning pre-language visual representations with adapted text across all184 outputs, including agentness. Frozen encoders receive no head-training gradients; both experts retain scene and language attention.
evidence: Scaled experts: triplet15.026 versus15.081; tail8.396 versus8.533; the latter alone does not establish a reliable semantic-language benefit. Lambda0.001. DCB is adapted from prior work and must be attributed.
action: Derive a focused gradient/loss panel from this small-encoder ancestor, updating scaled dimensions from code. Do not present the existing small-encoder figure as an exact scaled-expert diagram. Explain the local DCB reduction/history rather than silently equating it with the published formula.

title: Composition blending, selection and rejected routing complexity
why: Show why a fixed scalar blend was retained instead of a learned classwise or sample-dependent router.
caption: A fixed, selection-set-chosen alpha combines sigmoid composition scores from the two frozen experts. Primitive outputs follow the classification expert. The final semantic scores receive candidate confidence once. The inference blend is parameter-free after alpha selection and is not a sample-dependent gate.
evidence: Scaled blend versus classification: +0.722 triplet and +0.604 Tail47; versus contrastive: +0.667 and +0.468. Small-encoder focal global/classwise/generic/factorized triplet means12.584/12.590/12.588/12.593 do not demonstrate a meaningful routing advantage.
action: Use a compact scoring-and-selection diagram rather than another complete backbone drawing. Small-encoder DCB source is an ancestor, not the final scaled configuration. Keep gate negative results in an explicit comparison table.

title: What worked: controlled comparisons and frequency-stratified results
why: Connect each design decision to measured outcomes and distinguish architecture changes from encoder-system scaling.
caption: Detector frame-mAP at IoU0.5 on the locked ROAD-Waymo validation frames. Show individual seeds and mean±sample SD for matched studies; separate historical families and published external references. Tail47, Deep28 and Common39 use fixed training-derived membership.
evidence: Include mean-versus-attention, experts-versus-blend, focal-versus-DCB, scaled-versus-original system, and per-class gains/losses. DCB improves overall triplet but decreases Tail47 in the original-encoder comparison. Scaling changes both encoder checkpoints, projection and numerical extraction conditions.
